blurTest.evidence: At gallery scale the blue promise headline, real product screen, and short footer read in that order; inside the paywall, the upgrade title and lifetime action remain dominant.

silhouetteTest.evidence: The modal family shares one rounded glass silhouette with a white rim and soft shadow, while the App Store set keeps a consistent framed-device silhouette across phone and tablet.

fiveSecondTest.evidence: The hero communicates random winner selection immediately; the roster asset demonstrates the complete pool; the privacy asset states that no account is required.

realityTest.evidence: Every asset is composed from a rendered simulator screen. The supplied 18-name pool is preserved in order, including the repeated Olivia Rodrigo entry, and no fabricated testimonial or metric is shown.

journeyTest.evidence: The set covers entering names, adding the pool, choosing a mode, seeing a winner, reviewing recent winners, and deciding whether to unlock unlimited contestants.

platformTest.evidence: Screens were rendered on iPhone 17 Pro Max at 1320x2868 and iPad Pro 13-inch at 2064x2752, then placed into exact tracked 1284x2778 and 2048x2732 App Store canvases.

buyerValueTest.evidence: The assets communicate fast pool setup, no-repeat picking, winner visibility, no-account privacy, and monthly-versus-lifetime unlimited access without unsupported claims.

implementationTest.evidence: Debug and Release simulator builds succeeded. Screenshot seeding is DEBUG-only, the supplied names do not appear in the Release binary, and deterministic generation scripts reproduce the screenshot and marketing-asset sets.

screenFindings: Independent comparison against Tiny Decisions, Random Picker: Name Wheel, and Spin The Wheel confirmed the expected category cues: a dominant picking control, a concrete participant pool, and clear winner-state continuity.
The glass paywall now belongs to the same action-modal family as the winner, reset, clear, duplicate, sound, and no-repeat alerts rather than reading as a separate white sheet.
The refreshed marketing frames use rendered product pixels and concise benefit copy; no promotional headline or decorative device frame leaks into the in-app UI.
The complete supplied roster is legible in the phone details asset, with Julia Wolk used as the winner and the remaining captures maintaining the same pool context.
repairs: Extracted and applied a shared translucent action-modal surface with consistent corner radius, rim, shadow, and scale transition.
Reduced the standard paywall height to remove the former empty lower half while preserving Restore Purchases and legal links.
Added DEBUG-only deterministic screenshot fixtures and a repeatable iPhone/iPad capture script driven by external sample names.
Replaced six tracked legacy App Store marketing frames and raw source images with current rendered screens using the supplied roster.
Updated the screenshot shot list with the canonical 18-name sequence and preserved the intentional duplicate.
verdict: Approved. The action modal family is visually coherent, the paywall is compact and complete, the supplied names are represented in the refreshed phone and tablet App Store assets, and the production build remains free of screenshot fixture data.
